Overview

Tenable's FAQ on two vulnerabilities in Cursor (AI code editor) in how it handles MCP servers. CurXecute (CVE-2025-54135; CVSS 8.6 in the CVE record, 8.5 in Tenable's article), disclosed by AIM Security: through prompt injection — e.g. a crafted message read via a Slack MCP server — the agent rewrites the global mcp.json and so runs attacker commands. MCPoison (CVE-2025-54136, CVSS 7.2), disclosed by Check Point Research: once a user approves a project's MCP server, later changes to its configuration are trusted because approval is bound to the server's name, not its contents, so a malicious contributor can swap in a command. Both were reported in July 2025 through coordinated disclosure and fixed in Cursor 1.3.9 for CVE-2025-54135 and in Cursor 1.3 for CVE-2025-54136. The CVE records (CNA affected, cveawg.mitre.org) give the affected versions as earlier than 1.3.9 and earlier than 1.3; Tenable's table prints "1.21 and below" and "1.2.4 and below".
